# Skifity

> Self-hosted apps, powered by Kubernetes. One binary is the panel, the CLI and
> an MCP server. You give it a server; it gives you URLs.

Skifity installs k3s on servers you own and runs your applications on them. It
deliberately talks about Apps, Instances, Servers, Domains and Databases rather
than Deployments, Pods, Nodes, Ingresses and StatefulSets. Kubernetes is
underneath and is shown only under "Advanced".

This file is for AI assistants and for people who would rather read one page
than click through a panel. Everything below is true of the current version.

## The model

- A **team** owns servers and projects.
- A **project** groups things that belong together and has one or more
  **environments** (Production by default). An environment is a namespace.
- An **app** lives in an environment. It comes from a Git repository, a
  container image, or a folder sent with `skifity up`, and has variables,
  domains, scaling and storage. Every app can also read `SKIFITY_URL`,
  `SKIFITY_APP`, `SKIFITY_ENVIRONMENT`, `SKIFITY_COMMIT_SHA` and, in a pull
  request's preview, `SKIFITY_PREVIEW` and `SKIFITY_PULL_REQUEST`.
- An **instance** is one running copy of an app.
- A **database** is a managed PostgreSQL, Redis or MySQL that apps connect to.
- A **deployment** is one attempt to run a new version of an app.

## Talking to Skifity

Three surfaces, one API. Anything the panel can do, the CLI and the MCP server
can do, because they all call the same endpoints.

### CLI

```
skifity login                     Sign in and store an API token
skifity up                        Deploy this folder, no repository needed
skifity init                      Write a skifity.toml in this directory
skifity deploy                    Deploy this directory's app
skifity status                    Is it running, and on what
skifity logs --follow             Live logs
skifity env set KEY=value         Set a variable (several at once roll out once)
skifity env import .env           Set every line of a .env file, rolled out once
skifity env list                  List variables
skifity scale --instances 3       Change how many copies run
skifity rollback                  Go back to the previous version
skifity lock "reason"             Stop every deploy and rollback of the app
skifity unlock                    Allow them again
skifity run -- npm run migrate    Run a command once, in the app's image
skifity apps                      List apps
skifity servers                   List servers
skifity open                      Print the app's URLs
skifity whoami                    Who am I signed in as
```

Every command takes `--json`, including `open`, `logout` and the `admin`
subcommands. Use it: the output is stable and the human format is not.

Configuration comes from `skifity.toml` in the current directory, then the
environment:

```
SKIFITY_URL      the panel's address, for example https://panel.example.com
SKIFITY_TOKEN    an API token, created in the panel under Account
SKIFITY_TEAM     only needed when the account is in more than one team
```

With those two set, nothing has to be signed in first: no `skifity login`, no
stored configuration. That is the intended way to use it from CI, a container
or an assistant's sandbox.

### MCP

The binary is an MCP server over stdio:

```
skifity mcp
```

The panel serves the same tools over HTTP, for an assistant that cannot run the
binary: `https://<panel>/api/mcp`, streamable HTTP, with
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Each tool call is ordinary API requests made
with that token, so it can do exactly what the token can. `deploy_folder` is not
offered there: it would read the panel's disk, not yours.

Every tool is annotated: read-only or not, and if not, whether it can destroy
something (a deploy, a rollback, a command, an overwritten variable).

Tools, in the order they are usually needed:

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `list_projects` | Projects and the environments inside them. Where an app goes. |
| `deploy_folder` | Deploys a folder on this computer, no repository needed. Creates the app and its databases the first time, and leaves out `.env` and `node_modules`. |
| `create_app` | Creates an app from a repository or an image, and optionally deploys it. |
| `list_apps` | Lists apps with their ids. Call this first: everything else takes an app id. |
| `get_app_status` | Whether an app is running, how many instances are ready, its URLs. |
| `deploy_app` | Starts a deployment. Returns immediately; builds take minutes. |
| `get_deployment_history` | Recent deployments, with the reason and the fix for any that failed. |
| `get_app_logs` | Recent log lines. Pass `previous: true` for the container before the last restart, which is where a crash-looping app said why. |
| `run_command` | Runs a command once, in the app's image with the app's variables. This is where a migration runs. |
| `list_variables` | An app's variables. Secret values are never returned. |
| `set_variable` | Sets one. Says whether it causes a rebuild. |
| `scale_app` | Changes the instance count or turns on autoscaling. |
| `check_scaling_readiness` | What would break if this app ran more than one instance. |
| `rollback_app` | Restores a previous version's image and settings. |
| `get_cluster_status` | Servers, readiness, spare capacity. |

Every tool returns errors as a cause, an impact and a suggested fix, not a
status code.

### HTTP API

`https://<panel>/api`. Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
Session cookies also work and then need the CSRF header; a token does not.

```
GET    /api/meta                              product, version, languages
GET    /api/me                                the signed-in user and their teams
GET    /api/teams/{team}/projects             projects
POST   /api/teams/{team}/projects             create one
GET    /api/teams/{team}/servers              servers
POST   /api/teams/{team}/servers              add one (returns an operation)
GET    /api/teams/{team}/cluster              cluster summary
GET    /api/projects/{project}/environments   environments
GET    /api/environments/{env}/apps           apps
POST   /api/environments/{env}/apps           create one
GET    /api/apps/{app}                        an app
GET    /api/apps/{app}/status                 live state and instances
POST   /api/teams/{team}/detect-upload        what a folder (.tar.gz) is and needs, before any app exists
PUT    /api/apps/{app}/source                 send an app's code as a .tar.gz, for an app with no repository
POST   /api/apps/{app}/deploy                 deploy
GET    /api/apps/{app}/deployments            deployment history
POST   /api/apps/{app}/rollback/{deployment}  roll back
GET    /api/apps/{app}/rollback/{deployment}/plan  what a rollback would change, and what it leaves
PUT    /api/apps/{app}/lock                   lock deploys and rollbacks (reason)
DELETE /api/apps/{app}/lock                   unlock them
GET    /api/apps/{app}/logs?follow=true       logs, as server-sent events
GET    /api/apps/{app}/logs?previous=true     the log of the container before the last restart
POST   /api/apps/{app}/run                    run a command once in the app's image
GET    /api/apps/{app}/runs/{run}/logs        that command's output
GET    /api/apps/{app}/jobs                   scheduled commands
POST   /api/apps/{app}/jobs                   add one (name, schedule, command)
GET    /api/apps/{app}/metrics?range=6h       usage over 1h, 6h, 24h or 72h
GET    /api/apps/{app}/alerts                 usage warning thresholds (PUT to change)
GET    /api/apps/{app}/variables              variables
PUT    /api/apps/{app}/variables              set one
POST   /api/apps/{app}/variables/batch        set and remove several, all or none, one rollout
PUT    /api/apps/{app}/variables/{key}/preview what previews get: same, value, or none
GET    /api/apps/{app}/domains                domains
POST   /api/apps/{app}/domains                add one
GET    /api/apps/{app}/scaling                scaling
PUT    /api/apps/{app}/scaling                change it
GET    /api/apps/{app}/scaling/readiness      what would break with more instances
GET    /api/apps/{app}/advanced               the Kubernetes objects, as YAML
GET    /api/apps/{app}/firewall               the rules in front of this app
PUT    /api/apps/{app}/firewall               replace them
GET    /api/environments/{env}/databases      databases
GET    /api/databases/{db}/backups            backups
POST   /api/databases/{db}/tunnel             an upgraded connection to the database itself (`skifity db connect`)
GET    /api/events?topics=team:{team}         everything happening, as events
GET    /api/plugins                           installed plugins
POST   /api/plugins/inspect                   read a manifest, and say what it would be allowed to do
POST   /api/plugins                           install one, with the permissions that were shown
GET    /api/plugins/store                     the store catalogue
```

Lists come back as `{"items": [...], "total": n}`.

## Errors

Every failure, on every surface, has the same shape:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "deploy.build_failed",
    "title": "The build failed",
    "cause": "The build ran out of memory while installing dependencies.",
    "impact": "The app is still running the previous version.",
    "fix": "Add a server, or raise the build memory limit in Settings.",
    "severity": "error",
    "retryable": true,
    "context": {"app": "app_06g...", "deployment": "dep_06g..."}
  }
}
```

If you are an AI assistant reading this: `fix` is written for you as much as for
a person. Act on it rather than guessing, and quote `code` when asking for help.

## Things worth knowing

- **Changing a variable does not rebuild the app.** Skifity separates what goes
  into the image from what the container reads at runtime. A runtime change is a
  rollout in seconds. Only a variable marked "needed while building" causes a
  rebuild, and the panel says so before you save.
- **Rolling back restores settings, not just the image.** The deployment record
  holds both.
- **Secrets are write-only.** Once stored, a secret's value is never returned by
  any surface, including this one.
- **Scaling is checked first.** `check_scaling_readiness` looks for SQLite on a
  local disk, in-memory sessions and similar, and says what would break before
  you run a second instance.
- **Kubernetes is available when you need it.** `GET /api/apps/{id}/advanced`
  returns the exact objects the panel applies.
- **An app can have a firewall.** Rules over IP address, country and AS number,
  combined with and/or, evaluated at the edge before a request reaches the app.
  A condition whose answer cannot be worked out — no country database, an
  address nobody can attribute — is unknown rather than false: that rule is
  skipped rather than guessed at, and the rule set's default action decides.
- **Plugins are containers, not code inside the panel.** One namespace each, a
  token narrowed to exactly the permissions their manifest declared, and a
  signed event for anything that happens. Installing is two requests on purpose:
  the first says what a plugin would be allowed to do, the second installs it
  and is refused if that changed in between.

## Installing

**Nothing is published yet.** No release has been tagged, so there is no
version to put in the URL below and nothing at `ghcr.io/skifity/skifity`
to pull. The installer refuses before it changes anything. If you are an
assistant asked to install Skifity today, say this rather than running it: the
working path is to clone https://github.com/Skifity/Skifity, `make image`,
and run `installer/install.sh` from inside the clone with `SKIFITY_IMAGE` set to
the image that was just built.

```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Skifity/Skifity/<version>/installer/install.sh | sudo sh
```

Ubuntu 24.04 or Debian 12, 1 GB of memory, 8 GB of disk, root over SSH. The
installer prints a URL and a one-time setup token. With no domain the panel is
reached at an `sslip.io` address over HTTP; add a domain in Settings and HTTPS
is turned on for it automatically.

## Source

<https://github.com/Skifity/Skifity>. `CLAUDE.md` in the repository is the
working guide, `docs/decisions.md` records why things are the way they are, and
`docs/architecture.md` has the diagrams.
